ADR-037 register fragment — leaf-integrations. Declares Integriq's first OpenRegister integration leaves: `files`, `deck` and `talk` on `source`, `calendar` on `synchronization`. Four of the ~17 app-agnostic leaves, on 2 of 39 schemas; every other schema and leaf stays off, with reasons in openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-leaf-integrations/design.md.

WHY A FRAGMENT AND NOT AN EDIT TO integriq_register.json: InitializeRegister folds the md5 of every fragment into the version it hands importFromApp, so a fragment change forces the re-import that a base-file edit alone does not (importFromApp is version-gated on appinfo's version, which does not move between releases).

WHY `configuration.linkedTypes` AND NOT A TOP-LEVEL `linkedTypes`: Schema::hydrate() folds only `x-openregister-*` keys and `x-schema-org` into `configuration`. Every other top-level key is dispatched to a `set<Key>()` method, and a call to a method that does not exist is swallowed by hydrate's own catch — so a top-level `linkedTypes` imports cleanly, validates cleanly and is dropped on the floor without an error. Measured 2026-09-07; two schemas in a neighbouring app carry that shape.

WHY THE VERSIONS ARE BUMPED HERE: the importer only re-applies a stored schema when the incoming version is newer, or when ImportHandler::schemaContentDiffers() sees a change — and that method compares `properties`, `required`, `authorization` and `x-openregister-*` annotations only. A configuration-only change is invisible to it, so without a version bump this fragment imports and changes nothing, silently. Measured: the first import of this file landed (`imported_config_integriq_version` carried its fragment hash) while both schemas' stored `configuration` came back without `linkedTypes`. The stored `source` version had also drifted to 1.4.1 — OpenRegister increments the patch level itself on save — so the declared version has to clear the stored one, not the one 99-source-nested-auth-writeonly.json declares. This fragment sorts last among the fragments touching these two schemas, so its `version` is the effective one.

Declaring a leaf also adds a JSON column to the schema's magic table (MagicMapper::getLinkedTypeColumns; `files` is excluded because `_files` is already a metadata column), so this is a real schema change, not a UI flag. Leaves link entities held by other Nextcloud apps by object id and never read object properties, so nothing here widens the `source` credential surface that 99-source-lockdown.json closed.
